questions.prompt: Where does gas exchange take place in humans?
questions.why: Gas exchange occurs in the air sacs of the lungs.
questions.quote: In humans, gas exchange takes place at the air sacs.

questions.prompt: Compared with inhaled air, exhaled air contains less of which gas?
questions.why: Exhaled air has less oxygen than inhaled air.
questions.quote: Compared with inhaled air, exhaled air contains less oxygen, more carbon dioxide, more water vapour and has a higher temperature.

questions.prompt: Where does the oxygen in inhaled air go inside the air sacs?
options: It enters the blood in the capillaries
It is stored in air sacs
questions.why: Oxygen from inhaled air passes into the blood.
questions.quote: oxygen in the inhaled air enters the blood in the capillaries.

questions.prompt: What does the blood carry from body cells to the air sacs?
questions.why: Body cells release carbon dioxide, which the blood carries to the air sacs.
questions.quote: The blood carries carbon dioxide to the air sacs.

questions.prompt: In the path of air when breathing in, what does the trachea divide into?
questions.why: The trachea splits into two bronchi.
questions.quote: The trachea divides into two smaller tubes called bronchi.

questions.prompt: Which structure protects the lungs from injury?
questions.why: The rib cage shields the lungs.
questions.quote: The lungs are protected by the rib cage.

questions.prompt: Which process is the physical movement of air into and out of the lungs?
questions.why: Breathing is physical; respiration is chemical.
questions.quote: Breathing is the physical process of moving air into and out of the lungs.

questions.prompt: What does tar deposited in the lungs do to the air sacs?
options: It covers some of the surface
questions.why: Tar covers air sac surface and reduces gas exchange efficiency.
questions.quote: It covers some of the surface of the air sacs. As a result, the efficiency of gas exchange is reduced.

questions.prompt: What does carbon monoxide reduce?
questions.why: Carbon monoxide lowers blood's oxygen-carrying ability.
questions.quote: Carbon monoxide reduces the oxygen-carrying ability of blood.

questions.prompt: Approximately how many people die each year from smoking-related diseases?
questions.why: About 8 million people die each year from smoking-related diseases.
questions.quote: About 8 million people around the world die from diseases related to smoking each year.

questions.prompt: Inside the lungs, what do the bronchi further divide into?
questions.why: Bronchi divide into bronchioles inside the lungs.
questions.quote: the bronchi further divide into bronchioles

questions.prompt: How many air sacs are in the lungs?
questions.why: The lungs contain millions of tiny cup-shaped air sacs.
questions.quote: In the lungs, there are millions of tiny cup-shaped structures called air sacs.

questions.prompt: What are the surfaces of the air sacs covered with?
questions.why: Air sac surfaces are covered with capillaries.
questions.quote: Their surfaces are covered with capillaries.

questions.prompt: In the air sacs, what warms the air?
questions.why: Blood in the capillaries warms the air in the air sacs.
questions.quote: It is also warmed by the blood in the capillaries near the air sacs.

questions.prompt: Approximately what percentage of carbon dioxide is in exhaled air?
questions.why: Exhaled air contains about 4% carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: About how many air sacs are in our lungs?
questions.why: About 600 million air sacs are in our lungs.
questions.quote: There are about 600 million air sacs in our lungs.

questions.prompt: In emphysema, what happens to the walls of air sacs?
questions.why: In emphysema, the walls of air sacs are destroyed.
questions.quote: In emphysema, the walls of air sacs are destroyed and become less elastic.

questions.prompt: What narrows the bronchi and bronchioles in chronic bronchitis?
questions.why: Inflammation and excess mucus narrow the bronchi and bronchioles.
questions.quote: the bronchi and bronchioles become narrower due to inflammation and excess mucus secretion

questions.prompt: Which substance in cigarette smoke is addictive?
questions.why: Nicotine in cigarette smoke is addictive.
questions.quote: nicotine in cigarette smoke is addictive
